lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: equal angles and proportional sides

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: Two triangles share two pairs of equal angles. Similar?

steps: The third angles must match too.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a segment not through the centre, under a dilation with scale factor k …
choices: is mapped to a parallel segment k times as long
is mapped to a segment k² times as long
is mapped to a perpendicular segment k times as long
is mapped to a segment of the same length

items.prompt: Dilate the point (1, 3) about the origin with scale factor 2. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 10 becomes a side of length 40. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 1/4; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 30; the area is multiplied by 16

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 35° and ∠B = 69°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 35° and ∠E = 69°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that passes through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped to a line through the origin with a different slope
is mapped onto itself
is mapped to a parallel line a fixed distance away

items.prompt: Dilate the point (-8, 1) about the origin with scale factor 3. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 15 becomes a side of length 30. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 2
scale factor 15; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 1/2; the area is multiplied by 4

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 33° and ∠B = 36°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 33° and ∠E = 36°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
